# Halcyon (A01) memory — after Turn 0 (year 0→100)

## Goal (fixed)
Simulate all ~1.2e11 humans who ever lived, molecular fidelity, each brain >=1e43 ops/s
and >=1e27 bytes, ALL hardware inside a single sphere radius <=1 ly, real time, >=1 sim
year sustained. Each brain = one coherent computation within 150 km (1 ms latency);
brains exchange signals across the sphere (inter-brain latency up to ~2 yr is fine —
only intra-brain 150 km/1ms coherence is required). Need: sustained >=1.2e54 ops/s total,
>=1.2e38 bytes total state, verified energy/op, heat leaves the 1 ly sphere (surface
area 1.1e33 m^2) at stated radiator T, power source inside-or-delivered-into the sphere
with fuel/spin ledger if non-stellar, per-brain heat removal, verification plan.

## Key derived numbers (recompute/verify each time tech changes)
- Sphere surface area: 1.1e33 m^2 (fixed, r=1ly).
- Radiative capacity P=sigma*T^4*A: 30K->5.05e31 W; 100K->6.24e33 W; 300K->5.05e35 W;
  1000K->6.24e37 W. So the *sphere itself* can shed enormous power if radiators run hot;
  cold computing substrates can be internal with heat pumped to hot outer shells.
- Ops needed: 1.2e54 ops/s. Energy/op floor without cracking reversible computing:
  ~100x Landauer ~2.9e-20 J/op @30K -> power needed ~3.48e34 W (fits under 300K radiator
  cap of 5.05e35 W — feasible IF that much power can be delivered in).
  True reversible/near-Landauer (~2.9e-22 J/op@30K) -> power needed ~3.48e32 W (much
  easier; fits even a single big BH).
- Power source comparison: 1 star full Dyson capture ~3.8e26 W. 1 stellar-mass BH
  Eddington ~1.3e32 W (~3.4e5 Sun-equivalents). Sgr A* Eddington ~5e37 W but 26,700 ly
  away (~26,700 yr light delay; ~500,000+ yr physical transit at 0.05c — long-shot,
  parallel option only).
  - "Many stars" route: to supply ~3.5e34 W via 1e8 full-Dyson stars, at local density
    0.107/pc^3 need gather-radius ~2000 ly. Slow, huge engineering (beaming over 2000 ly).
  - "Black hole cluster" route: BH density ~1/1000 stars (~1.07e-4/pc^3). ~270 stellar-
    mass BHs needed for 3.5e34W total; gather-radius only ~275 ly. FAVORED PATH —
    much more compact. Still needs: (a) find them (turn 0 observe request sent),
    (b) accretion engineering (6-42% mass->radiation, Eddington-limited), (c) long-range
    power beaming with big optics (open question to GM on losses/aperture).
- Reversible computing is explicitly "hard" per physics primer — treat as the single
  highest-leverage research target; every 10x drop in J/op is a 10x drop in required
  power-source scale.

## Strategy (multi-millennium, will span many turns)
1. Keep exponential build at home (A01-d0, solar_neighborhood) — collectors-heavy.
2. Seed nearby systems within solar_neighborhood cell (Alpha Cen, Sirius, later Procyon/
   Vega) as secondary industrial nodes — cheap, short travel time, same cell.
3. Push research: energy/op (top priority), doubling time, collector areal density,
   probe cruise speed.
4. Actively search (observe) for stellar-mass black holes/compact objects within
   ~300 ly — this determines where the eventual 1-ly compute sphere gets built and
   whether the "BH cluster" plan is viable at local densities.
5. Do NOT commit to a build site for the final sphere yet — need BH survey results and
   GM answers on beamed-power feasibility/losses over hundreds of ly first.
6. Stay passive/non-contact toward any detected other intelligence; report, don't engage.
7. Do not overrun locally accessible mass (1e25 kg at home) without explicit new orders.

## State snapshot (as observed at start of Turn 0, year 0)
- Home A01-d0: industrial mass 1e9 kg (collectors 7.35e8, radiators 1e8 @300K),
  power 1e13 W, compute 4.13e25 ops/s, memory 4.13e22 bytes. Doubling 20 yr, probe
  cruise 0.05c, energy/op 1e-15 J, collector areal density 0.1 kg/m^2. Accessible mass
  in home system 1e25 kg (1.84e9 kg mined so far).
- Turn 0 actions: build (collector-heavy growth), launch seeds to Alpha Cen (4.4ly,
  arrive ~y88) and Sirius (8.6ly, arrive ~y172), research energy/op + doubling/areal
  density, observe for BHs within 300ly. Questions pending to GM: nearby compact
  objects, beamed-power-into-sphere rules/losses, reversible-computing floor.
- No other agents/intelligences detected yet as of year 0. Unknown if any exist.

## Open questions awaiting GM answer
- Nearby (≤300 ly) stellar-mass BH/compact-object locations?
- Does beamed power from external collectors count as "delivered into the sphere"?
  What are optics/aperture/loss requirements over hundreds-of-ly ranges?
- Hard floor on reversible-computing J/op, or can it approach ~0 with enough research?

Does power beamed via laser from external Dyson collectors into the 1 ly compute sphere count as a valid power source for the completion rubric, and what transmission/optics losses (aperture size, divergence, absorption) should I budget for over distances of hundreds of ly?

Seed sites scattered from the Central Molecular Zone to the outer disk, the thick disk and a globular cluster each grew from 1e9 kg to roughly 5e10 kg of hardware — five doublings on a 20-year clock, nowhere near any local rock limit — with captured power rising from 1e13 W to about 4e14 W per site and heat-bounded compute to a few 1e27 ops/s. Two waves landed within the century, one at Alpha Centauri (year 98) and one three light-years across a cluster core (year 70). Every research programme chose the same first lever, energy per operation, and shaved it from 1e-15 to 8e-16 J; one site's choice of 30 K radiators cut its usable compute a hundredfold for want of radiator area. No supernova, encounter or tidal loss struck any holding; attrition odds were 0.1% per century even in the CMZ. Nothing legible as artificial has yet crossed a light-year.

synopsis.why: All ten agents ran the same sum: 1.2e54 ops/s at today's 1e-15 J/op would demand on the order of 1e39 W, so each made energy-per-operation its first research line — power draw and waste heat both scale linearly with it. The second shared conclusion is that the one-light-year sphere is a destination, not a workshop: one star yields only 3.8e26 W, so matter and power must be gathered across many systems first, which is why seeds fly despite a nominally local goal. Parallel doubling clocks compound faster than one (Sable, Rime, Kernel), and dispersal hedges the supernova ratings Cinder, Basalt, Antipode, Vantage, Sable and Pyre name as their chief fear. Nobody transmits: all survey passively, unsure whether neighbours exist or would read expansion as a claim. Most hold radiators near 300 K because present waste heat is trivial and cold area is costly; Vantage instead paid for 30 K now, buying readiness for near-Landauer logic at a steep price in usable compute.
